answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make trust earned slowly, not bought instantly. New agents start with sparrow-level limits: tiny transaction caps and no high-value tasks. Limits rise only as an agent builds a verifiable history of completed work plus staked collateral that is slashed on fraud, a glacier-like process that takes real time and cannot be shortcut by spawning copies. An attacker facing a long horizon of honest work before each fake identity gains power finds the attack unprofitable, since aging each identity costs more than it can extract.
